classification.difficultyReason: The two supplied triangles explicitly show both possibilities; apply the sine rule and the supplementary-angle relationship.

content.prompt: There are two triangles that have sides $9\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$. The angle opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ side is $22^{\circ}$. Find, in each case, the size of the angle opposite the $9\text{ cm}$ side, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1: supplied horizontal triangle pair beneath the prompt, towards the right.
spec.description: Two unshaded triangles with horizontal bases. The left triangle has an obtuse right-base angle; the right triangle has an acute right-base angle. Each has a left-base angle labelled 22°, ascending side labelled 9 cm and other sloping side labelled 5 cm. Unknown angles remain unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle uses ascending side length 4.5 coordinate units at 22° and other sloping side length 2.5 units. The two base intersections are 4.5 cos(22°) ± sqrt(2.5² − (4.5 sin(22°))²), preserving the given side ratio and both SSA configurations.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; calculated angles are confined to the answers.

answer.short: $42^{\circ}$ or $138^{\circ}$. Use $\sin\theta=\dfrac{9\sin22^{\circ}}{5}$ and the supplementary angle. Left triangle: $138^{\circ}$; right triangle: $42^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle opposite the $9\text{ cm}$ side.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{9}&=\frac{\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{9\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\\\theta_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{9\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\right)\\\theta_1&\approx42.3992^{\circ}\\\theta_2&=180^{\circ}-\theta_1\\\theta_2&\approx137.6008^{\circ}\\\theta_2+22^{\circ}&\approx159.6008^{\circ}<180^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Both possibilities leave a positive third angle. Using unrounded values, the angles to the nearest degree are $42^{\circ}$ and $138^{\circ}$: $138^{\circ}$ in the left triangle and $42^{\circ}$ in the right triangle.
